newsitem.title: USA: Clinton maps legislative strategy with Democrats.
newsitem.headline: Clinton maps legislative strategy with Democrats.

text.p: President Clinton meets his Democratic congressional lieutenants at the White House Wednesday to discuss an array of budget issues and other politically delicate items on the legislative agenda.

Clinton and leaders of his party in the House and Senate were to gather in the Cabinet Room at 10:45 a.m. EDT to "kind of talk about where we are in implementing the budget agreement," White House spokesman Mike McCurry said.
The framework of a plan that would cut taxes and spending and balance the budget by 2002 was agreed on by the president and congressional Republicans May 2, but details are still being hammered out.
Many of Clinton's fellow Democrats are uneasy about the plan, believing it will eviscerate many of the social programs the party has fought for over the years.
McCurry said Thursday's meeting would "look at the timing and calendar that lies ahead as a result of the budget agreement, and talk about other legislative priorities the president has."
Clinton, who returned Monday from a week-long trip to Mexico, Costa Rica and the Carribbean, is also expected to solicit the leaders' views on proposals to curb so-called partial birth abortions.

The highly controversial procedure, also be referred to as dilation and extraction, involves the partial extraction of the fetus feet-first, the subsequent suctioning out of the fetal brain and removal of the fetus.

The Senate this week is likely to vote on a Republican proposal to ban such procedures except to save the life of the woman. But chief sponsor Rick Santorum, a Pennsylvania Republican, has acknowledged he is about five votes shy of a veto-proof 67 votes.
Clinton vetoed that measure last year and has vowed to do so again.

The White House said Tuesday it was "possible" Clinton could support a proposed compromise offered Senate Democratic leader Tom Daschle of South Dakota, which would waive the ban if a woman's life was in danger or she faced "grievous" physical health problems late in her pregnancy.
